/-!
# Explicit row-major encoding of the block ground set

Block coordinates are numbered by `block * width + coordinate`. The
equivalence connects compact machine-mask tables on `Fin (J*L)` with the
sigma-typed block sets in the reporting proof. Flattened one-hot coefficients
already include their positional radix factors.
-/

def coefficient {h J : ℕ} (o : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BlockEncoding.Occurrences h J) (b : Bool)
    (c : _root_.ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J (464*h)) : ℕ :=
  _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LocalCoverBounds.localPrime h ^ c.1.val * (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.GlobalEncoding.mapAt h (o c.1) (c.2,b)).val

def maskHash {h J : ℕ} (o : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BlockEncoding.Occurrences h J) (flip : Bool)
    (S : Finset (_root_.ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J (464*h))) : ℕ :=
  _root_.ThreeSum.OneHotMask.eval
    (_root_.ThreeSum.OneHotMask.extend (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BlockIndex.coefficient o flip ∘ (_root_.ThreeSum.BlockIndex.coordEquiv J (464*h)).symm))
    (_root_.ThreeSum.OneHotMask.extend (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BlockIndex.coefficient o (!flip) ∘ (_root_.ThreeSum.BlockIndex.coordEquiv J (464*h)).symm))
    (J*(464*h)) (_root_.ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.subsetMask (_root_.ThreeSum.BlockIndex.indexSet S))

The loop compares successive `4*(4*y)^(i+1)` with the radix. It returns

  _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.set 3 (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.k 16 *' _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.v 1) ;;
  _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.while (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.v 3 ≤' _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.v 0) (
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.set 3 (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.k 4 *' _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.v 1 *' _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.v 3) ;;
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.set 2 (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.v 2 +' _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.k 1)) ;;
  _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.set 0 (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.v 2)

# Merge sort

sort(n, a, fr) sorts the n cells from a in place, in ascending order (`sort_meets`).  It is the
recursive merge sort: sort the first ⌈n/2⌉ cells, sort the rest, merge the two halves into the n
cells from the free pointer fr, and copy them back.  It calls half, merge and copy.

The proof is an induction on n.  `body_ends` treats the body of the procedure, given that the
procedure sorts the lists of half the length, and `join_ends` its last two calls; `sorted_merge`
says that what the four calls leave is a sorted permutation of the list.  The number of steps,
`sortTime n`, is of the order n log n (`clog_split`, `time_split`), and the calls are nested
⌈log₂ n⌉ + 1 deep.  Numbers are only compared and copied, so their size does not matter.
-/

/-!
# From a solver of a task to a program for the layout of the end statement

A solver gets its size, the bound on the numbers and its addresses as arguments.  A problem of the
end statement has a fixed layout: cell 0 holds the size n, then comes the input, then the output;
the bound U = n^κ is not in the memory.  For every κ one more procedure, `topBody`, is appended to
the program of the solver.  It reads n.  At size 0 it answers at once.  Otherwise it forms U = n^κ
by κ multiplications and n², computes the addresses, calls the solver, and returns the result of
the solver (for a decision problem) or 1.

`Wrap` collects what has to be said about a problem and a task for this to work.  `Wrap.body_ends`
and `Wrap.body_ends_zero` follow the procedure through its text, `Wrap.small` bounds the word size,
the memory and the depth that the run needs by a polynomial in n, and `Wrap.realized` is the
conclusion: if the task is solved in time T, then the problem is solved on the word RAM within a
constant times T.
-/
